title: The spiral car park

data.source: Poincare (1895); the path-lifting theorem as in Hatcher (2002); cited from memory. Computed and simulated, seeded.

prediction: R2's lift is the unique lift of covering-space theory; cut times are unchanged by any shift along the line, deck transformation or not; turning the line round changes the count; every cut is the same point of the half-size circle; and for a closed loop the count is at least twice the winding number but not fixed by it (I also predicted the two would agree in fewer than half of forward-winding loops; that part missed).
baseline: Covering spaces: unique path lifting, deck transformations and monodromy (Poincare 1895; Hatcher 2002). Decoy: count = twice the winding number.
relation: identical to path lifting; the count lives on the covering line and uses its order, which the covering does not supply
status_line: CRR here is: a renaming of the lift of a path to the covering line; the cut rule then uses only differences and the line's direction, so it does not see the circle's own symmetry.
why: R2's 'unwrapped path' (Phoenix status ASSUMPTION) is the unique lift that covering-space theory gives, and it came back exactly from a record kept only on the circle. The cut times did not change under any shift along the line, so they depend on the lift and not on where the circle's seam is. Reversing the line changed the count, which is extra structure. Every cut sat at one point of the circle of half the length. For closed loops the winding number gave a lower bound on the count and nothing more, as the room ma-winding-number found.
